_about: Hand-curated from official Indian government documents. Each entry says what a type of event is officially described as leading to. It is general guidance for that type of event, not a forecast for any location. Edit this file to add entries; every entry needs an institution, a title and a link.

entries.label: Heavy to extremely heavy rain
leads_to: Localised landslides, mudslides and landslips in hilly areas
consequences: Damage to plantation, horticulture and standing crops
Partial damage to vulnerable structures; minor damage to kutcha houses, huts and roads
Road and rail traffic may be affected

source.title: National Bulletin No. 7, 8 Sep 2025, section 'Impact Expected' for very heavy / extremely heavy rainfall

entries.label: Cyclone
leads_to: Storm surge above the normal tide along the coast (warned separately by IMD)
Inundation of low-lying coastal areas from heavy rain and flash floods
Localised flooding of roads and water logging in low-lying areas
Riverine flooding in some river catchments
consequences: Damage to paddy, horticultural and standing crops from inundation and winds
Disruption of traffic from water logging and squally or gale winds

source.title: National Bulletin No. 37, 30 Nov 2025, cyclone warning: storm surge warning and 'Impact Expected'

entries.label: Glacial lake
leads_to: Glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) and related flash floods, which NDMA names as a serious risk to vulnerable mountain communities
entries.note: Being in the inventory does not mean this lake is hazardous. Whether a particular lake could breach needs a lake-specific study; the inventory does not say.

source.title: Guidelines on Management of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), Oct 2020 (summary on PreventionWeb)
